es.summary: Obstrucción súbita de una arteria pulmonar por un trombo, generalmente proveniente de una trombosis venosa profunda. Es una emergencia que compromete el intercambio gaseoso y la perfusión tisular.
key_points: Obstrucción súbita de arteria pulmonar por trombo de TVP
Disnea y taquicardia repentinas son signos cardinales
Diagnóstico rápido con angio‑TC y D‑dímero
Anticoagulación es tratamiento de primera línea
Complicaciones graves: hipertensión pulmonar, shock y muerte
Cuidado de enfermería: monitorizar signos vitales y signos de sangrado

pathophysiology: Formación de trombo en vena profunda (TVP)
Desprendimiento y embolización al árbol arterial pulmonar
Obstrucción parcial o total de arteria pulmonar
Aumento de resistencia vascular pulmonar → hipertensión pulmonar aguda
Compromiso del intercambio gaseoso y disminución del gasto cardíaco
signs_symptoms: Disnea súbita, empeora con el esfuerzo
Dolor torácico pleurítico, a veces hemoptisis
diagnostics: Angio‑TC pulmonar: defecto de llenado en arteria
Gammagrafía de ventilación/perfusión: déficit de perfusión
Gasometría arterial: PaO2 < 80 mmHg, PaCO2 variable
ECG: taquicardia sinusal, signos de sobrecarga derecha
treatment: Anticoagulación: heparina no fraccionada o enoxaparina
Anticoagulación oral: warfarina o DOAC (rivaroxabán, apixabán)
Trombolisis en casos de alto riesgo hemodinámico
Embolectomía quirúrgica o por catéter si falla anticoagulación
nursing_care: Monitorizar signos vitales cada 15‑30 min (PA, FC, FR, SatO2)
Evaluar nivel de conciencia y dolor torácico
Mantener vía aérea permeable; administrar O₂ por máscara o cánula nasal
Preparar al paciente para estudios de imagen
patient_teaching: Explicar importancia de la anticoagulación y adherencia
Enseñar signos de sangrado y cuándo reportar
Instruir sobre movilización temprana y ejercicios de piernas
Advertir evitar viajes largos sin mover piernas
Informar signos de recaída (disnea, dolor torácico)

care_plans.diagnosis: Riesgo de disminución de la perfusión tisular cardíaca
outcomes: Mantener saturación de O₂ ≥ 95% en reposo

interventions.action: Evaluar signos vitales, especialmente presión arterial y frecuencia cardíaca, cada hora
interventions.rationale: Detectar hipotensión o taquicardia que indiquen disminución de perfusión

interventions.action: Monitorizar saturación de oxígeno y administrar oxígeno suplementario según necesidad
interventions.rationale: Mantener adecuada oxigenación tisular

interventions.action: Observar signos de sangrado (hematuria, hematomas) por anticoagulación
interventions.rationale: Prevenir complicaciones hemorrágicas que empeoren perfusión

interventions.action: Mantener hidratación adecuada vía oral o IV según indicación
interventions.rationale: Evitar hipovolemia que reduzca gasto cardíaco

interventions.action: Colaborar con el equipo para iniciar anticoagulación según prescripción
interventions.rationale: Prevenir crecimiento del trombo y mejorar perfusión

related_to: fatiga al realizar actividades de la vida diaria
evidenced_by: disnea al caminar menos de 100 metros
fatiga al realizar actividades de la vida diaria
outcomes: Incrementar distancia de marcha a 200 m sin disnea
Reducir frecuencia cardíaca al final de la actividad a < 100 lpm

interventions.action: Evaluar nivel de disnea antes y después de la actividad usando escala de Borg
interventions.rationale: Cuantificar tolerancia y guiar progresión

interventions.action: Planificar actividades graduales, iniciar con ejercicios de rango de movimiento y caminar 50 m
interventions.rationale: Mejorar capacidad funcional sin sobrecargar el corazón

interventions.action: Enseñar técnicas de respiración diafragmática y control de ritmo
interventions.rationale: Reducir sensación de falta de aire

interventions.action: Monitorear frecuencia cardíaca y saturación durante la actividad
interventions.rationale: Detectar intolerancia temprana

interventions.action: Proveer reposo entre actividades y posicionar al paciente semi‑sentado
interventions.rationale: Optimizar ventilación y perfusión

interventions.action: Educar al paciente sobre la importancia de reportar dolor torácico o síncope
interventions.rationale: Prevenir complicaciones graves

en.summary: Sudden obstruction of a pulmonary artery by a thrombus, usually originating from deep venous thrombosis. It is an emergency that compromises gas exchange and tissue perfusion.
key_points: Sudden obstruction of pulmonary artery by DVT thrombus
Sudden dyspnea and tachycardia are cardinal signs
Rapid diagnosis with CT angiography and D‑dimer
Severe complications: pulmonary hypertension, shock, death
Nursing care: monitor vital signs and bleeding signs

pathophysiology: Detachment and embolization into pulmonary arterial tree
Partial or total obstruction of pulmonary artery
Increased pulmonary vascular resistance → acute pulmonary hypertension
Compromise of gas exchange and decreased cardiac output
diagnostics: Pulmonary CT angiography: filling defect in artery
Arterial blood gas: PaO2 < 80 mmHg, PaCO2 variable
ECG: sinus tachycardia, signs of right‑sided overload
treatment: Oral anticoagulation: warfarin or DOAC (rivaroxaban, apixaban)
Surgical or catheter embolectomy if anticoagulation fails
nursing_care: Monitor vital signs every 15‑30 min (BP, HR, RR, SatO2)
Assess level of consciousness and chest pain
Maintain airway patency; administer O₂ via mask or nasal cannula
Monitor for bleeding due to anticoagulation
patient_teaching: Explain importance of anticoagulation and adherence
Teach signs of bleeding and when to report
Instruct on early mobilization and leg exercises
Warn against long trips without moving legs
Inform signs of recurrence (dyspnea, chest pain)

care_plans.diagnosis: Risk for decreased cardiac tissue perfusion

interventions.action: Assess vital signs, especially blood pressure and heart rate, hourly
interventions.rationale: Detect hypotension or tachycardia indicating decreased perfusion

interventions.action: Monitor oxygen saturation and administer supplemental oxygen as needed
interventions.rationale: Maintain adequate tissue oxygenation

interventions.action: Observe for bleeding signs (hematuria, bruising) due to anticoagulation
interventions.rationale: Prevent hemorrhagic complications that worsen perfusion

interventions.action: Maintain adequate hydration orally or IV as indicated
interventions.rationale: Avoid hypovolemia that reduces cardiac output

interventions.action: Collaborate with team to initiate anticoagulation per prescription
interventions.rationale: Prevent thrombus growth and improve perfusion

related_to: fatigue during activities of daily living
evidenced_by: fatigue during activities of daily living
outcomes: Increase walking distance to 200 m without dyspnea
Reduce heart rate at end of activity to < 100 bpm

interventions.action: Assess level of dyspnea before and after activity using Borg scale
interventions.rationale: Quantify tolerance and guide progression

interventions.action: Plan gradual activities, start with range‑of‑motion exercises and 50 m walk
interventions.rationale: Improve functional capacity without overloading heart

interventions.action: Teach diaphragmatic breathing techniques and rhythm control
interventions.rationale: Reduce sensation of breathlessness

interventions.action: Monitor heart rate and saturation during activity
interventions.rationale: Detect early intolerance

interventions.action: Provide rest between activities and position patient semi‑upright
interventions.rationale: Optimize ventilation and perfusion

interventions.action: Educate patient on importance of reporting chest pain or syncope
interventions.rationale: Prevent serious complications

summary.0.quote: The clot is usually a deep vein thrombosis (DVT), a clot in the leg.

key_points.0.quote: A pulmonary embolism (PE) is a sudden blockage in a lung artery.

sections.pathophysiology.0.quote: The clot is usually a deep vein thrombosis (DVT), a clot in the leg.

sections.pathophysiology.1.quote: The cause is usually a blood clot that breaks loose and travels through the bloodstream to the lungs.

sections.risk_factors.1.quote: Anyone can get a pulmonary embolism (PE), but certain things can raise your risk of PE: Having surgery, especially joint replacement surgery.

sections.risk_factors.6.quote: Certain genetic changes that can increase your risk of blood clots and PE. Obesity .

sections.signs_symptoms.1.quote: Symptoms of PE include: Shortness of breath Rapid breathing Chest pain or discomfort, which usually gets worse when you cough or take a deep breath Increased heart rate Coughing up blood Very low blood pressure, lightheadedness, or fainting Sometimes people with PE don't have any symptoms until they have serious complications, such as pulmonary hypertension (high blood pressure in the arteries to your lungs).

sections.signs_symptoms.4.quote: In the blood vessels, baroreceptors can become less sensitive with aging, causing dizziness or orthostatic hypotension .

sections.treatment.4.quote: Administer oxygen therapy to maintain oxygen saturation > 92 percent.

sections.nursing_care.3.quote: They can cause bleeding, especially if you are taking other medicines that also thin your blood, such as aspirin.

sections.patient_teaching.3.quote: Moving your legs when sitting for long periods of time (such as on long trips).
